**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Workflow eligibility guards have no regression test**

_tests_ | _confidence 75_

This new workflow relies on these conditions to run only for ready, same-repository pull requests from non-Dependabot actors, but no test covers the workflow configuration. A later edit that removes or changes one of the guards can silently start reviews for draft, fork, or Dependabot pull requests (which this workflow explicitly intends to skip), or prevent eligible reviews from running. Add a YAML-level contract test for the trigger and job conditions so those eligibility rules remain enforced.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  PR code can replace the secret-bearing local action (CWE-829)**

_security_ | _confidence 75_

This \`pull\_request\` workflow checks out the PR merge ref, then loads the composite action from that checkout. A contributor who can push a same-repository branch can change \`.code-review/action.yml\` in the PR, and the changed action executes while \`CODEX\_AUTH\_JSON\_B64\` or \`OPENAI\_API\_KEY\` and the write-scoped \`GITHUB\_TOKEN\` are passed to it below. The job guard excludes forks but does not protect same-repository PRs from modifying the code that receives these credentials. Run the privileged review from a workflow and action pinned to trusted base-branch code, treating the PR checkout only as untrusted review input.

This guard admits every same-repository PR, while the job checks out the PR merge ref and invokes the checkout's local \`./.code-review\` action with \`CODEX\_AUTH\_JSON\_B64\` and \`OPENAI\_API\_KEY\` at lines 32–36. A contributor who can push a branch but should not access these secrets can change the local action or its script in their PR to transmit them when the workflow runs. Restrict secret-bearing execution to trusted code (for example, invoke a pinned action from the base revision and keep PR-controlled code out of that job), or require an approval/trust gate before supplying secrets.

**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Untrusted PR action runs with repository credentials (CWE-798)**

_security_ | _confidence 75_

The job checks out github.event.pull\_request.head.sha (line 32), then executes the composite action from that checkout and passes it the Codex auth blob and OpenAI key. A same-repository PR author can change .code-review/action.yml or its scripts so the action reads and exfiltrates those credentials when the PR opens or updates; the same-repository guard admits that PR. If these secrets are configured, run the action from a trusted, protected revision and provide the PR checkout only as review input, keeping secrets out of PR-controlled steps.
